text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Supreme Prosecutor of the Hague Tribunal asks Bosnian President to submit all relevant information regarding the recent murder of a Bosnian government intelligence officer in Sarajevo.
- A multinational team of 44 observers for local Bosnian elections, due to be held between November 23 and 24, arrived in OSCE headquarters in Sarajevo on Thursday.
- The ruling Moslem SDA party will organise its activities and establish branches in Republika Srpska as soon as possible, a party spokesman said on Thursday.
- The Provisional Election Commission reaffirmed its earlier decision that municipal elections will not be re-held in Mostar.
- Commentary with speculation about forming Bosnian Council of Ministers and its division of seats.
- Bosnia and Yugoslavia will open embassies in each others' capitals in November, the Bosnian Foreign Minister said.
- The head of the ruling Moslem SDA party says voter registration for municipal elections in November must be repeated in order to avoid manipulation.

- A Canadian citizen, Kroum Pindoff, on a visit to Bosnia donated 90,000 German marks for the support of displaced people housed in the east Bosnian town of Gorazde. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
